title: Harden command guardrails and make terminal process-exit tests reliable.
changes: Reject catastrophic shell commands hidden behind argument-taking wrappers such as sudo, nice, ionice, timeout, and env split-string when the runtime is in restricted mode.
Preserve legitimate wrapper commands and include negative regression tests without executing destructive operations.
Verify the exit status of a short-lived process after its initial stdout, avoiding an unreliable expectation of synchronous completion.

Preserve the existing 84-tool runtime surface, explicit local God Mode behavior, per-device ownership, and current public API contracts. The guardrail remains defense in depth rather than a shell sandbox; unrestricted agents still require least-privilege rollout.
Require coordinated public npm packages and signed release artifacts before merging this runtime into the private production branch.
